explain.say: About four and a half thousand years ago, builders at Mohenjo-daro in the Indus valley made fired bricks in neat proportions of four to two to one, and some of their walls still stand. Bricks remain one of the most loved building materials. On the board, a modern brick cavity wall cut open, outside on the left, the warm room on the right.

explain.say: Bricks are clay fired at around a thousand degrees. Laid in a bond, each brick overlaps the joints below, so loads spread and the wall acts as one. A standard brick is two hundred and fifteen by sixty five millimetres on its face; add ten millimetres of mortar and you need about sixty per square metre of half-brick wall. Which bond looks strongest to you?

English bond, with its rows of headers tying the wall through! Now strength. Engineering bricks can carry over a hundred megapascals, but see how weak the mortar is, around four. That is on purpose: cracks run through soft mortar, easy to repair, not through bricks. A two hundred and thirty millimetre wall at half a megapascal carries a hundred and fifteen kilonewtons per metre.

explain.say: Back to the cavity wall. Rain soaking through the outer leaf meets the air gap and runs down, never reaching the inside. Steel ties bridge the gap so both leaves work together. The insulation board slows heat, so the whole wall loses only about a quarter of a watt per square metre for each degree of difference. Which layer stops the rain?

explain.say: The air cavity! At the bottom, a damp-proof course, a plastic strip in a mortar joint, stops water rising up from the ground. Great work! Exam tip: for brick counts, always add the mortar joint to the brick size. Challenge: how many bricks would you order for ten square metres of half-brick wall?

faq.q: How many bricks are in a square metre of wall?
faq.a: For a half-brick wall with standard 215 by 65 millimetre bricks and 10 millimetre joints, one brick covers 225 by 75 millimetres, so about 60 bricks per square metre, plus a few percent for waste.

faq.q: What is the difference between English and Flemish bond?
faq.a: English bond alternates whole courses of headers and stretchers. Flemish bond alternates headers and stretchers within every course. Both tie a one-brick wall through its thickness.

faq.q: Why is mortar weaker than brick?
faq.a: Mortar is made weaker on purpose so that movement and cracks happen in the joints, which are easy to repoint, instead of splitting the bricks.
Two leaves of masonry with a gap between them, joined by metal wall ties. The cavity stops rain crossing to the inner leaf, and insulation in it keeps heat in.
asks: How does a cavity wall work?

faq.a: A waterproof layer, usually a plastic strip laid in a mortar joint about 150 millimetres above the ground, that stops moisture rising up a wall from the soil.

facts: Bricks at Mohenjo-daro in the Indus Valley followed proportions of about 4 : 2 : 1.
A UK standard brick measures 215 × 102.5 × 65 mm.
Engineering bricks are graded class A (at least 125 MPa) and class B (at least 75 MPa).

quiz.say: At about 60 bricks per square metre, how many bricks are needed for 10 square metres of half-brick wall?
quiz.show: About how many bricks are needed for 10 m² of half-brick wall (60 per m²)?
quiz.why: 10 m² × 60 bricks per m² = 600 bricks, plus a little for waste.

wrong.1: That is for only one square metre.
wrong.2: That slips a factor of ten.

quiz.say: In a cavity wall, what stops rain reaching the inner leaf?
quiz.show: In a cavity wall, what stops rain reaching the inner leaf?
quiz.why: Water that gets through the outer leaf runs down the cavity instead of crossing it.

wrong.2: Ties are shaped with drips so water does not cross them; they do not stop rain themselves.
